source.label: Restored from source
source.desc: Its rules, numbers and words come straight from the original server code Tiny Speck released.

rebuilt.label: Rebuilt from footage
rebuilt.desc: The rules survive but the level or art does not, so it is reconstructed from gameplay recordings.

reimagined.label: Reimagined
reimagined.desc: Nothing about it survives, so it is designed fresh in the spirit of the original.

solo.label: Adapted for solo play
solo.desc: A multiplayer system reworked so one player can enjoy it: rival Glitches, companions, a hired hand.

lost.label: Can't come back
lost.desc: Nothing about it survives, or Tiny Speck retired it before Glitch closed.

groups.name: The world
groups.blurb: Streets, hubs and the physics of getting around Ur.

groups.name: Creatures & trees
groups.blurb: Piggies, chickens, butterflies, trants and the things that roam.

groups.name: Gathering & making
groups.blurb: Gardens, mining, cooking, machines: the crafting economy.

groups.name: Giants & economy
groups.blurb: Quoins, currants, vendors, shrines and imagination.

groups.name: Quests & adventures
groups.blurb: Story quests, quest rooms, races and Paradise.

groups.name: Home & neighbours
groups.blurb: Houses, furniture, mail and the people next door.

groups.name: Late game
groups.blurb: Rooks, Icons, the Rube, skills and the long tail.

items.name: Original streets
items.blurb: Over 1,400 archived streets with their real geometry, layered art, parallax, colour grading and signposts.

items.name: Doors, ladders and walls
items.blurb: Doors between streets, climbable ladders and solid walls restored from the location files, keys included.

items.name: Glitch physics
items.blurb: The client’s walk, jump, Triple Jump, ladder and air rules, plus each street’s own physics (underwater, low gravity, tiny).

items.name: Street scripts and puzzles
items.blurb: Archived street event scripts run again; puzzle streets got their lost switches and triggers rebuilt. Shim Shiri’s Light Beams are clicked to Beam Up into the gut tubes.

items.name: Dametime and the day cycle
items.blurb: The official calendar: ten-second minutes, four-hour days, eight-day weeks, and a new day that refreshes Ur.

items.name: Hub maps and travel
items.blurb: Every region’s map with its streets. Travel by signpost; from the map, set a destination for a guided path, or with Teleportation IV teleport to a street you have visited.

items.name: The Ur subway
items.blurb: Twelve stations under Ur on one loop, the Red Line one way and the Blue Line the other. Go down the station stairs on Gregarious Grange, Groddle Forest Junction or any of the other ten, push A Red Button for a 50-currant ticket (Your Papers must be in order), ride, and get off at any stop or stay on for the next. Ride counts earn Subwayfarer, Ground Hogger, Commuter Mug and Chute Jockey. The fares, lines, announcements, gate and badges come from the source; the stations and the train were never archived, so they are rebuilt from players’ footage with Tiny Speck’s own subway art. With nobody else to wait for, the train leaves ten seconds after you board.

items.name: Music and sounds
items.blurb: The published soundtrack per region, every recovered Musicblock and meditation track, Esquibeth's melody from her own overlay files, real recordings for most sound keys (Wayback files plus Tiny Speck's archived sound effects set), and gentle synth stand-ins for the sounds still lost.

items.name: Your Glitch
items.blurb: Tiny Speck’s own vector avatar, rebuilt part by part: walk, climb, jump, happy, angry, surprised, with real hair, eyes, mouths, hats and clothes in their original colourways, sharp on Retina. Start fresh with Tiny Speck’s new-player picker, four choices for each part, or dress up as a giant, the Rook or a chicken from the original wardrobe. Nineteen pieces Tiny Speck left in greyscale are reimagined with colours borrowed from their siblings, and tagged as such. A player’s 2012 sheets, found on the Wayback Machine, were the first reference for the poses; they stay in the research notes and never ship.

items.name: Camera Mode
items.blurb: Press C to look around the street; with Eyeballery, the whole street.

items.name: The new-player tutorial
items.blurb: An optional start: fall through the clouds, learn to walk and jump with the Welcoming Flamingo and the Dustbunny, get your home street and first skill, buy two bags on Gentle Island, go home for the Magic Rock's send-off, and head out into Ur.

items.name: Eleven Secret Locations
items.blurb: Twenty DNAja-vu beacons across Ur, a Giant’s message at each, and Lem’s at the eleventh.

items.name: The hidden floors
items.blurb: Three rooms no signpost leads to, each behind its street’s own hidden teleporter: the lost floor off Goorsh Gam’s treetops, the forgotten floor up in Odena Odes’ ceiling, and the missing floor at the top of Ilmenskie’s cave mouth, a running Triple Jump off the mushroom caps. The lost and missing floors are rebuilt from players’ footage and Snaps with Tiny Speck’s own apartment-hall art: ripped posters, dripping pipes, a climbable vine.

items.name: Vicar’s Peak
items.blurb: The Groddle Heights cliff behind Thornfad Layers’ locked door (Door Key 1): seven tiers of pebbly ledges, wooden ladders twined with vines, and a stone-arched door at the top that leads on to Mossystep. Home to 11 Piggies, 7 Chickens and a Metal Rock, as its loading card said. Its layout was never archived, so it is a reconstruction from a 2011 party recording and two players’ 2012 Snaps, built with Tiny Speck’s own Heights art.

items.name: The Ancestral Lands
items.blurb: Baqala, Choru, Zhambu and Xalanga weigh on you: Overwhelming Ancestral Nostalgia gives you 10 minutes a visit (11 and 12 with the two Prepared For Ancestral Nostalgia cards), Dust Trap remnants and Ancestral Spirits buy time back, and time away wins half of it back. Run out and you are Overwhelmed: sent to a street beyond the savanna and kept out for half an hour. The longer you stay, the bolder the Juju Bandits get.

items.name: Piggies
items.blurb: Pet, nibble for meat, feed, name, capture and incubate, with the exact Animal Kinship tables; piggies keep a mood and hunger, sulk in gloomy places and wander over to eat dropped food.
items.multiplayer: A street Piggy is everyone’s: its mood, hunger and daily clock, and who petted, nibbled or fed it, are kept by the server, and a hungry one eats a tree’s fruit in front of everyone; a server restart keeps them.

items.name: Chickens
items.blurb: Squeeze for grain, incubate eggs, raise chicks.

items.name: Butterflies
items.blurb: Massage with lotion, then milk; the onboarding quests start here.

items.name: Trants and Wood Trees
items.blurb: Six living trees to pet, water and harvest (with super harvests), Wood Trees for planks, and Tree Poison: a poisoned tree dies into a dead tree you clear and replant.
items.multiplayer: Trees are shared by everyone on the street: a harvest by anyone wears a Wood Tree down, and a tree the Rook rooks loses its fruit for everyone until it is revived. Tree Poison, its antidote and a tree’s death are everyone’s too: a poisoned tree dies for the whole street, and its Planks fall for the one who poured it. A tree’s poison, its death and the Rook’s damage survive a server restart.

items.name: Batterflies and guano
items.blurb: Cave Batterflies that turn food into guano, and the bar that boosts them.

items.name: Foxes and Heli Kitties
items.blurb: Fox brushing in the preserves and the kitties overhead.
items.multiplayer: A preserve’s foxes and baits are everyone’s there: one fox comes for every three players on the street, so ten players can see four at once and all earn Fox Flurrier. A fox three players have brushed runs off for everyone, and eight players past the Ranger fill the preserve.

items.name: Crabs
items.blurb: Crabs on eight streets will listen to your Musicblocks, and one that hears its oldest tune is a happy crab. Flatter one and hug it for Crabato Juice. Play a crab the tune it just heard and it still shouts and sulks, but solo you keep the block: the original destroyed it, which only made sense with other players in between. In multiplayer the crab keeps it, as in the original.

items.name: Animals, trees and shrines tell their stories
items.blurb: Walk up to a chicken, piggy, butterfly, tree, rock, peat bog, barnacle, patch, shrine or Icon and it may call you over with something to tell. All 92 of their conversations come word for word from the source, offered by its rules: one every half hour, every 15 seconds while you are in the middle of a chain, and none until you have given to every shrine. Forty-three of them lead up to the shrines, whose stories wake the Street Spirits’ own. A talk cut off by a reload picks up where it stopped.

items.name: Who lives where
items.blurb: Each street’s real population of animals, trees, rocks and shrines from the archive.

items.name: Gardens and herbs
items.blurb: Hoe, plant, water and harvest crops and herbs, with the Master Gardener potions.

items.name: Mining and metal
items.blurb: Mine four rock types, smelt, grind and make metal with the original tools. Other Glitches sometimes work a rock near you: Help mine it for I Me Mine, and when they join your rock each one adds to what you get.
items.multiplayer: Rocks are shared by everyone on the street, and real players can help each other mine for more chunks.

items.name: Cooking and making
items.blurb: The recipe catalog across every making tool, with skill rules and tool wear.

items.name: Powders
items.blurb: Every Beaker powder does its own thing again: No-No Powder’s rush and crash, Sneezing and Sparkle Powder, the Fecundity powders that make the animals drop their edibles, Fertilidust for the trees (it brings dead ones back to life), and hallowed powder that doubles or triples your next shrine donation. In multiplayer, Sneezing and Sparkle Powder reach every other player on the street.
items.multiplayer: Sneezing Powder and Sparkle Powder spread to the other players on your street.

items.name: Potions
items.blurb: Every Cauldron potion can be quaffed or poured again: the Amorous Philtre’s Feeling Called Love, the Elixir of Avarice’s fifty extra quoins, favor from a Draught of Giant Amicability (shake it for another Giant), the Keycutter Tonic, Potions of Animal Youth, clouds that embiggen or shrink you, Rainbow Juice that sends you up, and Trantsformation Fluid that turns one tree into another. You can munch a Rug, too.

items.name: Machines and the Still
items.blurb: Assemble Blockmakers, Fuelmakers and Woodworkers; fuel them; distil hooch.

items.name: Peat, dirt, jellisacs and more
items.blurb: Harvestable street resources and their rare drops.
items.multiplayer: Peat, dirt, jellisacs and the other resources are shared by everyone on the street: what one player takes is gone for the rest, and players can help each other dig a Dirt Pile for more Earth and Loam.

items.name: Tools that wear and mend
items.blurb: Every tool’s exact condition, breakage and Tinkertool repairs.

items.name: Quoins
items.blurb: All eight quoin types, daily limits, multipliers and Qurazy quoins. Each street quoin spot is given one of the original quoin classes, which sets what it gives (a tiny 1, a small 2 to 6, a steady 25, a long-wait 2 to 100) and how long it takes to come back. Grab an iMG, mood, energy or currants quoin near other Glitches and they get a shard, and their grabs near you share with you. In multiplayer a street’s quoins are shared: the first to touch one gets it.
items.multiplayer: A street’s quoins are shared by everyone on it: the first player to touch one gets it.

items.name: Giants and shrines
items.blurb: Donate at the eleven Giants’ shrines for favor; a waiting emblem is handed over as you walk past, and the third shrine you pass says hello. Spend favor, or a spare emblem, to learn the skill you are studying faster.

items.name: Bureaucratic Halls
items.blurb: The hall doors on Gregarious Grange, Chego Chase and Baeli Bray open again: the Bureaucratic Hall, the Andra and the Muufo halls, where the bureaucrats behind the counter sell the Card-Carrying Qualification, Your Papers and General Building Permits. The halls themselves were never archived, so all three use the one hall rebuilt for Legalize It. Every hall has its Water Cooler; a Cup of Water tastes bureaucratic-y and brings on Being Watched.

items.name: Bags and the 16-slot pack
items.blurb: The pack holds 16 stacks; Generic and Bigger Bags, Toolboxes, the Spice Rack, Alchemistry Kit, Cubimal Case and Elemental Pouch add their own slots and open above the pack. A full pack refuses pickups and vendor buys with the original words, and the magic rock holds anything else until there is room. Online characters made before bags were given starter bags through the ledger, once.

items.name: Street spirits and vendors
items.blurb: The original stores, stock and prices, buying and selling. The scarecrow Gardening Tools Vendor, the Meal Vendor, the Tool Vendor, Uncle Friendly, Helga and the Sno Cone Vending Machine stand on the eleven streets the archive puts them on, each with its own store, and the scarecrow sends you on his Meet the Merchants errands. Sno Cones give iMG, not energy: each colour needs its level, the fourth of the day may freeze your brain, and a dropped cone melts. A Street Spirit you have not visited for a game day may get lonely: it calls you from the corner of the screen in its porthole, asks to be your destination, cries on its street until you walk up to it, and thanks you with 1000 iMG, or throws you a party.

items.name: Imagination upgrades
items.blurb: The upgrade card shop with its hand of three cards, re-deals and effects.

items.name: Levels, energy and mood
items.blurb: The official XP table, level rewards, metabolics, idle mood loss and food variety.

items.name: Badges
items.blurb: The full badge catalog with official art and the original counters.

items.name: Trading and giving between players
items.blurb: In multiplayer, trade items and currants face to face with another player on your street, up to six stacks a side as in the original: the server holds both offers until you both accept, and the site settles the swap so only what you really hold can change hands. Or give a stack, a written note or a wrapped Gift Box to a player beside you; the site moves it from your ledger to theirs, and they unwrap the box.
items.multiplayer: Trade face to face, or give a stack, a written note or a wrapped Gift Box to a player on your street, or drag a pack item onto them to give it. Drop a stack on a public street and everyone there sees it; once you have walked away from it, whoever picks it up first has it. Make a trade offer from the Menu and everyone on the street, and anyone who arrives, hears you are looking for someone to trade with for five minutes; Start negotiation! opens the trade.

items.name: Auction house
items.blurb: In multiplayer, sell a stack to other players for the price you name, and browse, search and buy what they list, at the original’s prices: a non-refundable 1.5% listing fee (at least 3 currants), 8% commission on a sale, 72 hours to sell. Bought, cancelled and expired stacks come by mail from the Auction Fulfillment and Logistics Corporation ten minutes later. The auction pages were never released, so the Auctions window is drawn new.
items.multiplayer: List, browse, search and buy between real players; the site holds every listing and moves the stacks and currants through the ledger.

items.name: Story and skill quests
items.blurb: Hundreds of original quests with their dialogue, offered by the Magic Rock or, where the original had one, their own giver: your Butler, the Ghost of Gwendolyn, the Greeterbot.
items.multiplayer: The quests that need other players are offered between real players: bootlegging Hooch, handing out Teleportation Scripts, kind gifts, tending, watering and gifting a friend’s home, meditating and radiating together, digging a Dirt Pile together (It Takes Two), and each race challenge goes in the challenger’s quest log.

items.name: Quest rooms
items.blurb: Private quest instances: almost none survive, so each is rebuilt from the quest code and gameplay footage.

items.name: Hand-built story quests
items.blurb: Phantom Glitch, Rooks’ Woods, Museum of the Rook, Winter Walk, A Summer’s Day, Ilmenskie Jones, Legalize It and more.

items.name: The Purple Journey
items.blurb: Imbibe an Essence of Purple and wait: the minute of HURRY UP PLEASE ITS TIME, then Le Voyage Violet, where Scions of Purple say strange things and quoins appear. Purpled Out follows, and three journeys earn Elementary Penguin. The room was never archived, so it is rebuilt from the players’ Snaps.

items.name: Ticket to Paradise
items.blurb: Thirteen private courses: Cloud Rings, Radial Heights, Starlit Night, Slip ’N Slide, Aerial Boost, Mountain Scaling, Abysmal Thrill, Arbor Hollow, Bippity Bop, Cloud Flight, Updraft, Sky Plunge and Drafty Uplift. Tiny Speck built Updraft and Drafty Uplift, but they may never have reached players: only eleven Paradise courses are known to have gone live.

items.name: Races and Game of Crowns
items.blurb: Seven race courses rebuilt from footage, raced against recovered rival Glitches under the final ticket-race rules. In multiplayer, Grab ’Em Good, the seven finish-line races and the Game of Crowns are against the real players on your street.
items.multiplayer: Grab ’Em Good, the seven finish-line races, The Great Hog Haul and the Game of Crowns (four players, the crown, tags and locks decided by the server) are played against the real players on your street; a reload mid-race ends it for both, as a logout did. A reload during a Game of Crowns takes you out while the others play on, and nobody races from Naraka.

items.name: The Great Hog Haul
items.blurb: The piggy-wrangling race, on its real cave street, against a rival.
items.multiplayer: In multiplayer the ticket challenges the real players on your street, the server decides every sack, Piggy and pen delivery, and the challenge puts The Great Hog Haul in your quest log, finished when you win.

items.name: Street projects
items.blurb: Build new streets and upgrades together. In multiplayer everyone on the street fills the same phases, the site takes what you give from your pack, rewards follow the original shares and top contributors, and a finished street opens its road for everyone. Solo has a hired hand.
items.multiplayer: Everyone on a street fills the same project, a finished street opens its road for everyone, and a group can claim one of the ten group halls and build it as its own.

items.name: Feats
items.blurb: The Last Feat’s incantation chain and ten of the old Feats. In multiplayer one Feat a day is shared by everyone playing: a live bar with its minimum, bonus and supermegabonus goals, contributors ranked, petrified rocks by place and the top-contributor badges. Solo keeps them as goals of your own, each worth a Small Petrified Rock and open again a game week later, with local companions taking the chain’s other parts.
items.multiplayer: One Feat a day is shared by everyone playing, with its goals, the contributors ranked and the top-contributor badges. The 13 who put in most get a Large Petrified Rock.

items.name: Party spaces
items.blurb: All eight party packs and their party streets. In multiplayer a pack opens one space for your whole party: everyone gets a way in, shares the clock, the Party ATM and the quoins, and the creator can kick someone out.
items.multiplayer: A Party Pack opens one party space for your whole party, with a shared clock, Party ATM and quoins, kept through a server restart; a space that can’t go on gives back what it cost.

items.name: The Smuggler
items.blurb: Carry Contraband across Ur without a Deimaginator catching you, then break the wrongfully imprisoned Smuggler out of his cell.

items.name: Holidays
items.blurb: Zilloween, Glitchmas and Pi Day on their dates, and the Egg Hunt all year from Egg Plants.

items.name: Your house and yard
items.blurb: Get your house and home street free, as in 2012: the Magic Rock hands you a Home Street Ticket and the Home Street Selection Machine takes it for a Meadow, Firebog or Uralia street. Paper it wall by wall with Tiny Speck’s own 109 wallpapers, floors and ceilings, decorate rooms, cultivate the street and the private back yard left of the house (walk out through the house’s open end; worn-out rocks, gardens and patches become protos you restore with a project), expand both (the yard from 5 to 20 segments, which with a full-width street earns Landgrabber), restyle the street as any of 36 of the original 37 street styles and the back yard as any of 34 of its 37 (Change Style, level x 10 iMG; each rebuilt from Tiny Speck’s own scenery, a yard drawn like the street of its template family), keep animals. A Butler arrives in a box, stitched part by part from Tiny Speck’s own pieces (choose its head, face, accessory, body, arms and legs), to greet you home, hold what neighbours leave, invite you to join the club and hear about it, and swap daily hi signs with you (press 5; outrun its hi for the evasion badges). Add a second and third floor with a Door (the Furniture Store, or recipe 260): set it on your top floor and put 100 Planks into Build a New Floor. Give any piece a new style in Decorate: the original’s 565 furniture upgrades in Tiny Speck’s own art, 113 of them free and the 452 that cost credits sold for currants instead, at 1,000 currants a credit (reimagined: the going rate players sold credit furniture at in the 2012 Marketplace forum), so a 15 credit Chair style is 15,000 currants; Bonus Furniture Upgrade I to III turn 5% of the furniture you make into a style that cost credits.

items.name: Mail
items.blurb: Mailboxes, postage, parcels and replies. A letter with an item comes by AFLC Frog, and the Mail Dispatcher outside your World Gate sends parcels.

items.name: Neighbours
items.blurb: Visiting Stones lead to six authored neighbours, standing in for other players’ homes.
items.multiplayer: Visit other players’ homes as they keep them, knock to be let in, give friends house keys, leave a package or a message with their Butler, and water and tend their gardens with their key. Put up to five friends’ homes on your home street’s signpost, post a note on a Note Pole for visitors to read, sell furniture to visitors (the price waits in a Pile of Currants), and restore a friend’s worn-out cultivations together.

items.name: Your Tower
items.blurb: Cultivate a Tower on your home street, build it as a project, pick one of six styles and every floor, roof and decoration the original offered, and raise it to nine floors marked L to 8 on the elevator, each decorated on its own; every new floor goes up at a Workbench on a planked frame open to the stars. The Jethimadh Tower Base hides eleven secret spots.

items.name: Craftybot
items.blurb: A crafting robot delivered in a box by your Magic Rock: queue jobs and it fetches the ingredients and tools, crafts every step, burns fuel and crystals, and hands you the results.

items.name: Other players and chat
items.blurb: Make a character with an email and a password, right in the game, and finish it from the link we email you; in multiplayer you share the street with other players: see them walk and emote, chat on the street, form a party with its own chat, keep buddies (who is online and where) and block players. Global Chat, Live Help and the Trade Channel are open to everyone the original let in, and players make, find and join groups with their own chat. Say hi with 5 and your daily hi sign flies to another player; a player with no sign catches it, matching signs share a bonus, and the clock shows the day’s Hi sign leaderboard. Follow another player and your Glitch walks after them wherever they go, teleports included.
items.multiplayer: See other players and chat on the street, form parties, keep buddies, join groups and channels, trade hi signs, and follow another player from street to street. Hug, high five, kiss, moon or splank another player from their menu, soak them with a Watering Can or play them a Musicblock, play Charades on the street (the first to say your word wins), and throw a house party big enough for Epic Blowout.

items.name: Rook attacks
items.blurb: The herald, the attack, stuns with the Focusing Orb, primed shrines and the revival. In multiplayer, everyone on the street fights the same Rook together.
items.multiplayer: Everyone on the street fights the same Rook together.

items.name: Skills
items.blurb: All 105 skills to learn, with the real effects where their systems exist.

items.name: Better Learning
items.blurb: Better Learning I to V, skills from 2011 that the late game retired, are back with their 2011 learn times in proportion (1 minute up to about 10.6 hours at the late game’s study speed): each rank cuts the time of every skill you learn after it by 2, 5, 8, 12 and then 20%, the third needs an Emblem of Lem, and learning them opens their favor quests and the street project work that asks for them. In 2011 they also raised a 20-skill limit. That limit is not here, the late game’s Brain Capacity cards stay, so that half of them is reimagined.

items.name: Meditation and teleportation
items.blurb: Focusing Orb meditation, levitation, teleport points and scripts.
items.multiplayer: Transcendental Radiation works between real players: radiate calm to everyone near you, the Transcendental cards widen and lengthen it, and meditating players show their orb to the street.

items.name: Giant Icons
items.blurb: Make an Icon from eleven emblems and tend it for the Giants’ love.

items.name: The Rube
items.blurb: The mysterious trader who appears and offers a swap.

items.name: Hell (Naraka)
items.blurb: Croak and work your way out by squishing grapes, or step into the Hell Bar behind Panka Surazu, where Hell’s Bartender swaps a Diabolical Drink Ticket for Wine of the Dead.

items.name: Musicblocks, Cubimals and the Stoot doll
items.blurb: All 27 recovered Musicblock tunes (five series of five, SB-1 and Goodnight Groddle) with their collector trophies, both Cubimal series and the memorial pull-string doll.

items.name: Fortune Cookies, Plates of Beans and other small things
items.blurb: Put a written note in a Fortune Cookie and break it for a Fortune to read, type /beans in Local chat for a Plate of Beans to overthink (again and again, each time with one more "really"), turn a Great Hog Haul Ticket into the Hog Haul, chop Wood Trees with the Class Axe, and hit the Balls on Plexus and Nandu Pitha. Their verbs, words, numbers and art come from the source. Only the three numbers behind the Ball’s hit survive, not what the game did with them, so the way it flies and bounces is reimagined.

items.name: Artifacts and petrified rocks
items.blurb: Crack a petrified rock with a pick, hoe, hatchet, shovel or grinder for artifact pieces, necklace beads, a gem and currants; a whole set rebuilds one of the ten artifacts or five necklaces. The rocks were Feat rewards: each of your own Feats gives a Small one, and again every game week, so a set or two comes with time.

items.name: Door Drink portals
items.blurb: Pour a Door Drink and a Hyperspacetime Portal Door stands at your feet. The original chained everyone’s doors across Ur; here the chain is yours, so each new door leads back to the one you poured before it.

items.name: Snapshots
items.blurb: With the Snapshottery card, press Enter in Camera Mode to take a Snap and caption it; your Snaps live on the site.
items.multiplayer: A Camera from the Toy Vendor shows a random Snap by another player and takes you to where it was taken.

buckets.label: Playable
buckets.note: Offered and finishable in the remake.

buckets.label: Street projects
buckets.note: Build-a-street jobs: counted under Street projects.

buckets.label: Still being rebuilt
buckets.note: Their rooms or systems are on the workbench.

buckets.label: Needed other players
buckets.note: Multiplayer races and favours between players.

buckets.label: Retired before shutdown
buckets.note: Tests, removed features, broken or unreachable in the original.

rooms.title: An Autumn Day
rooms.offer: As you may or may not know, many choices lack a right or wrong answer.

note.tagline: A silhouette memory of drifting words.
note.about: An Autumn Day, the sequel to A Summer's Day, was a short shared memory of the Giants: a black-on-sunset wood and a feeling to recall.
note.play: Follow the crow, climb the floating words, and jump into the scrambled sentence to put "Almost forgot this feeling of …" back together. The last word picks a feeling room with a hidden Qurazy quoin.
note.source: The four linked places, the five-minute limit, the leave flag and the hourly repeat; the original AUTUMN_DAY music.
note.rebuilt: Layout and puzzle rebuilt from Lily Linguistic's recording; the feeling rooms beyond Wonder are drawn from their names. Players' Snaps give the backdrop every room shares: three hazy layers of gnarled trees with red leaf puffs (Tiny Speck's own limbo trees), two bare saplings, red bushes and a heavy vignette.

rooms.title: An Old Fashioned B&E
rooms.offer: Psst … I figured out how to get in.

note.tagline: Rotate pipe tiles to break into the lab.
note.about: An Old Fashioned B&E had you sneak into a pale lab maze, with a voice over the speakers promising cheese.
note.play: Press the wall buttons to rotate pipe tiles until a path opens, climb the ladders, reach the end box, and drop through to a room of quoins that is, sadly, not cheese.
note.source: The five-minute limit, the exit flag and both reward sets.
note.rebuilt: The speaker's lines are transcribed from GranniesgotGame's recording; the tile puzzle is reconstructed around the lab seen there.

rooms.title: Being Watched
rooms.offer: Umm, You don't look so good.

note.tagline: A beige dream and something behind the veil.
note.about: Being Watched began with a stale cup of water and a nap, and a dream where eyes follow you everywhere.
note.play: Hop across pillow clouds past blinking wall eyes, peek behind the veil, and find out who has been watching.
note.source: The five-minute nap, the Peek Behind the Veil and Ride It Out flags, and the rewards.
note.rebuilt: No footage or layout survives, so the dream is reimagined; the Bureaucrat's three lines behind the veil are new writing.

rooms.title: Carry That Weight
rooms.offer: friend! You're going to help us whether you like it or not!

note.tagline: Dig up the Juju bandits' clues across Kajuu.
note.about: Carry That Weight sent you to the Juju Bandits' hideout, where Grandma sets you hunting for her lost Ancestral Paperweight with secret clues.
note.play: Hear Grandma's briefing, take the trowel and the first hint, then read each riddle to find the right street in Kajuu and dig there. Three clues lead to the Paperweight; bring it back to her for Part II.
note.source: Grandma's conversations, the clue table (four hubs × five streets), the grandson's scene and its lines, the 20 archived dig spots and the rewards.
note.rebuilt: The hideout's geometry was lost. Four players' Snaps show it at dusk, so it is built from the camp's own decos under a mauve sky: two teepees, Grandma's tall wooden chair, stacks of paper, the campfire and a dirt mound.

rooms.title: Color Unblocking
rooms.offer: You look like a fashionable young glitch. "On trend", "in-the-know", so to speak.

note.tagline: Wall switches that make coloured blocks vanish.
note.about: Color Unblocking was the first of the colour puzzle levels: switches on the wall turn coloured felt blocks on and off, and you have to clear a path to the exit.
note.play: Press switches to remove red, yellow, blue and charcoal towers in the right order; one switch also drops a bridge, so order matters. Through the door, a thank-you page from the level designer. The first finish earns the Play Cube, which lets you replay every puzzle level.
note.source: The five-minute limit, the exit flag, the crab at the end, the 250 iMG / 100 energy / 50 Ti favor reward and the Play Cube.
note.rebuilt: The level's layout and switch scripts were lost; it is rebuilt from the level designer's run-throughs with the original switch art. Players' Snaps give the look: a white void, felt blocks, a charcoal felt floor, the purple door and Keita Takahashi's finale drawing, which survives as Tiny Speck's own art.

rooms.title: firefly_whistle
rooms.offer: In the future of one of our pasts, the last days of the Alphite Age, some radical technologists had developed advanced techniques for the charming of fireflies.

note.tagline: A whistle behind a force field, and no way home.
note.about: Firefly Whistle sent you back to a past future, the last days of the Alphite Age, to learn how its radical technologists charmed Fireflies. Bump into a Firefly and the Magic Rock offers it, with a warning: you must find your own way back.
note.play: Walk the Fireflex 3000 Lab to the Precious Equipment Protection Unit, push its button to drop the force field and take the whistle, which you promptly swallow. Then talk the Teleporter Control Unit into switching on (it will drop hints) and step onto the pad. You feel woozy and fall a long way, past giant numbers counting down to 29, until you land and are beamed home. From then on a Firefly Jar opened near Fireflies sets your whistling instinct off.
note.source: The offer, the Firefly's "What ho! ... Fireflies!", every line from the stand, the whistle and the control unit with its six hints and activation code, the swallow (hit, hit, surprise, "Gah. I've swallowed it!", the Firefly Whistling badge), the walk back at the midpoint, the pad's push-back, the arrival point, the teleporter's position, the three-minute "Are you stuck?" prompt, the reward and the jar's badge gate. The pad sends you to the falling room ("You Feel Woooooozy..."), whose hidden teleporter takes you back to where you started.
note.rebuilt: The lab's geometry was never archived. It is rebuilt from three players' Snaps of it and a player's recording of the whole quest, which fixes the room's ends, where the stand, the walk-back point and the control unit stand, and the order along the corridor: an entry doorway with a ramp, windows, G2 signs, four pillars you walk behind, the "Church of Alph" poster, one egg-shaped phone pod and hanging security orbs. It is dressed entirely in Tiny Speck's own lab art from the starter set: walls with their G2 signs, windows, deck, doorway, pillars, posters, cables, notes, the "Tii Saves" graffiti, and the stand, control unit, teleporter, egg pod and orbs. The falling room is lost too; the same recording and three Snaps show it built from Tiny Speck's Headroom decos, so it uses those: the two number columns, ray bursts, bubbles, the tongue you land on, coral, flowers and glyphs. The recording is reference only.

rooms.title: Gwendolyn's Task
rooms.offer: Hear me. I am Gwendolyn, disciple of Cosma, daughter of Egeria, drowned as I lived in the waters of Grendaline’s Rising.

note.tagline: A desert, a mind in space, and a ghost.
note.about: Gwendolyn's Task is a three-part journey set by the ghost of Gwendolyn: survive the desert heat of Area 42, walk through your own mind, and find her chamber.
note.play: Follow the squid through the scorching desert, climb the pink tube path of the Outer Mind, cross the crystal Inner Mind, and meet Gwendolyn for a Random Kindness.
note.source: Area 42 survives and runs on its real street; the heat, the desert script, the cactus and squid dialogue and the rewards are original.
note.rebuilt: The Outer Mind, Inner Mind and chamber are rebuilt from three runthrough recordings.

rooms.title: Join the Club
rooms.offer: Welcome home friend.  While you were away, you received an intriguing invitation. It appears you've been invited to join the club.

note.tagline: Only the observant may enter.
note.about: Join the Club invited you to the Society of Keen-Eyed Noticers, whose treehouse door opens only for those who notice things.
note.play: Climb the treehouses, find the burnt sketch in each, set the clubhouse frames to match and press ENTER. Inside, jump into the Curious Painting for a bonus meadow of Qurazy quoins.
note.source: The five-minute clock, the painting's reach, the wall buttons' reset time, the flags and rewards.
note.rebuilt: Layout and puzzle rebuilt from SnygystFS's recording; only one sketch was readable in it, so the decoys are new.

rooms.title: Le Misérable
rooms.offer: Do you remember the future of one of our pasts? Or was it the past of one of our futures?

note.tagline: Light panels, a shrink ray and a crawl space.
note.about: Le Misérable took place in the Fireflex 3000 Lab: match three light panels to switch on a machine, shrink yourself, and crawl through to the other side.
note.play: Step on floor pads to cycle each column of lights until the panels match their answers, then ride the shrinking beam, crawl under the low walls and grow back. MaintenanceBot M-64 hands out both parts.
note.source: The lab is one of only two rooms that survived. It runs the street's own 234 event scripts; only the lost pads, reset buttons and machines are rebuilt around them.
note.rebuilt: The pads, buttons and machines were items whose positions were lost, placed from the circle marks on the floor and the recording.

footage.label: Le Miserable and A Summer’s Day

rooms.title: Mental Block
rooms.offer: Everything ok? You seem somewhat puzzled.

note.tagline: Drop blocks from a tube to build a way up.
note.about: Mental Block and its sequel were block-drop puzzles: build a staircase to a high ledge from a fixed sequence of blocks.
note.play: At each station, move the tube and drop blocks in order. Blue blocks stack on anything; red ones stack only on red and crush the blue beneath. Reset if you box yourself in.
note.source: The flags, rewards and the "Are you stuck?" prompt (not a timer: the sequel takes longer than five minutes).
note.rebuilt: Each station's block order, tube stops and ledge heights are measured from the level designer's two videos.

rooms.title: Mr. Block's playroom
rooms.offer: Hey, kid. How do you feel about getting small?

note.tagline: Spell words for Mr. Block in a tiny playroom.
note.about: Child's Play and Word Up shrank you into Mr. Block's playroom. First you bring him something starting with his letter, then you spin letter blocks into as many words as you can.
note.play: Give Mr. Block an item whose name starts with his letter. In Word Up, spin three letter blocks for three minutes; the more of the 24 words you find, the bigger the bonus. A plush tea party carries on in the corner.
note.source: The letter rule, the 24-word list, the reward tiers at 3, 10 and 20 words, and the tea party's exact lines.
note.rebuilt: The room's geometry was lost; players' Snaps show a giant child's bedroom, so it is furnished with Tiny Speck's own Kid's Room set (bed, panda, tea party, crayons, sneaker) around the recovered letter blocks and Mr. Block.

rooms.title: Operation: Grow
rooms.offer: So dark.

note.tagline: Bring a gloomy bog back to bloom.
note.about: Operation: Grow sent you to Mab's forgotten bog fields to make the blue grow again.
note.play: Tend the seven gloomy patches; each tends its neighbours too. Mab's note by the big hut shows the only answer. Then climb down the ladder into the root tunnel, where a pot under each patch glows once it blooms, and walk out past the EXIT.
note.source: The spawn point, five-minute limit, flags and rewards.
note.rebuilt: The room was never archived and its puzzle is designed from the quest text. Four players' Snaps show the place: a dusky field of stalks between Firebog bottletree huts over a root tunnel with teal pots hanging from its ceiling, tangled roots and an EXIT. It is built from Tiny Speck's own Firebog pieces, and the stalks turn blue as they bloom.

rooms.title: Picto-Pattern
rooms.offer: Pop Quiz! How many Giants are there?

note.tagline: Add and subtract until you reach 11.
note.about: Picto-Pattern was a number puzzle: turn a starting number into 11 in a set number of steps, using tally-mark clouds.
note.play: At each of three stations, press the coloured step buttons to fill a chain of clouds. A wrong total flashes red and empties; the right one turns the chain into walkable clouds that lead on.
note.source: The five-minute limit, the target of 11, the solved and leave flags, and the reward of 11 Cloud 11 Smoothies.
note.rebuilt: The three puzzles (14 in three steps, 8 in four, 1 in six) are taken from the level designer's run-through; tally marks are drawn fresh. Two players' Snaps show it is felt craft, so the clouds are Tiny Speck's own stitched felt clouds and the ground their felt grass, recoloured to the Snaps' pale green.

rooms.title: Radiant Glare
rooms.offer: Young Glitch, you once walked toward the light, proving your eyes are sharp. But, without practice, your skills may become dull.

note.tagline: Climb a dark shaft by mixing coloured light.
note.about: Radiant Glare was a vertical light puzzle: platforms only exist in light of their own colour.
note.play: Touch orbs to light timed lamps, mix colours on a two-bank console (yellow and blue make green), and use the "clicking on it works just as well" totem to reach the rainbow and the exit.
note.source: The five-minute limit, flags and rewards for both the quest and its replay.
note.rebuilt: Rebuilt from the level designer's run-through; the lamps' timings are measured from the video.

rooms.title: Rainbow Run
rooms.offer: Psst.

note.tagline: 30 coins in 30 seconds in a psychedelic night meadow.
note.about: The Numismatic Hustle dropped you into a private Rainbow Run: grab thirty coins before a thirty-second clock runs out.
note.play: Click Ready, sit through the 3-2-1, then sprint across the meadow and hop the broken columns for coins. Up the rainbow slide, pink islands and stairs lead into a sliced planet for more. Thirty or more and the rainbow is yours; fewer and the quest fails so you can try again.
note.source: The ready screen, countdown, 30-second clock, coin counter, success and failure lines, and the FUTURE_SWING_30 cue.
note.rebuilt: The course's layout was never archived. Four players' Snaps show the look, so it is built from Tiny Speck's own pieces: a black starry sky over a purple band, lime hills, a giant stone head on its side and a giant foot, a peace-sign hand, slimy broken columns to stand on, pink floating islands and stairs, a rainbow slide and a sliced planet with a door. The route is fitted to the remake's jump, with 56 coins, 38 of them on the meadow.

rooms.title: Smuggle the Smuggler
rooms.offer: I've got a job that needs doing. A dangerous job that needs doing.

note.tagline: Break the Smuggler out of jail.
note.about: Smuggle the Smuggler followed the contraband runs: the Smuggler has been locked up, and you have to dig him out.
note.play: Talk to the imprisoned Smuggler, dig through the patch with a shovel, and crawl out to freedom together.
note.source: The three quests' dialogue, flags, the shovel requirement and the rewards.
note.rebuilt: The cell's layout is lost; it is built from the recovered penalty-box decos.

rooms.title: The High Jumper
rooms.offer: You know that poem in the beginning of The Great Gatsby?

note.tagline: The Magic Rock's memory of a very tall tree.
note.about: The High Jumper sent you into the Magic Rock's memory-place: a white void with one enormous tree whose branches are too far apart to jump.
note.play: Pick up Spinach, activate it from your pack for its jump boost, and climb the alternating branches to the top. The Rock nags if you forget the Spinach.
note.source: The two-minute visit, the Rock's lines ("Trial and error, baby. Just get started…") and its 30 and 45 second nags, the free energy, and the top_of_tree flag.
note.rebuilt: The tree is rebuilt from the GlitchAddict recording with recovered branch and trunk decos; each gap needs the Spinach jump. A player's Snap gives the look (pure white, a flared root base) and the place's own name, The Gold Hatted, Bouncing, High Jumping Memory Place.

rooms.title: The Last Pilgrimage of Esquibeth
rooms.offer: Kid, you now know a little something about the Giants. You’ve matured. I think you are ready to contribute to a Feat.

note.tagline: Walk Esquibeth's last pilgrimage and learn her song.
note.about: The Last Pilgrimage of Esquibeth retold a Glitch legend: follow her ghost through grottos and up a waterfall, collecting notes and replaying her song at each Giant stone.
note.play: Find the notes, then play back the ghost's melody (click or keys 1 to 5). At the top, Esquibeth dances, Grendaline appears, and you keep the Conch as a memento.
note.source: The quest rules and rewards, the Conch's Play and Blow, the Hollow's own background painting, and the melody Esquibeth's ghost plays at each stone, all from Tiny Speck's overlay files.
note.rebuilt: Narration was read from two full recordings, and her song (E G D, E C, A D) was matched from their audio against the recovered bell sounds. Each grotto's sky colour is sampled from players' Snaps and a recording: peach-pink, pale lemon with a pink flush, magenta-pink.

rooms.title: The Wrizzards and The Rube
rooms.offer: Hey friend! Wanna make a tra … I mean, do you wanna help me out?

note.tagline: Catch ten Wrizzards hiding in The Rube's yard.
note.about: The Wrizzards and The Rube had you search the mysterious trader's yard for ten escaped Wrizzards.
note.play: Search the junk garden (behind the toadstool, the jars, the tree roots, the bird bath and the rook skull) and click each Wrizzard; it hops back into The Rube's jar.
note.source: The five-minute limit, the ten-Wrizzard counter and the 500 iMG / 500 currants / 100 mood reward.
note.rebuilt: The yard's geometry and the Wrizzard art were lost. Two players' Snaps show a dusky junk garden, so it is dressed with Tiny Speck's own Groddle and Firebog decos; the Wrizzards are lizard decos in a wizard hat.

rooms.title: Vision Quest
rooms.offer: So you like looking at things, right? And I hear with your mastery of Eyeballery, you’re pretty good at it too.

note.tagline: Help a short-sighted frog pass his eye test.
note.about: In the Institute of Ocular Testing, the Myopic Delivery Frog needs to name an object across the room to join the delivery service, and he cannot see it.
note.play: Press C for Camera Mode, look across the room at the mystery object, then talk to the frog and pick the right description. Wrong answers get his glasses offered; the right one sends him flying off happy.
note.source: This room survives in the archive, so it runs on the real Institute street. The six possible objects, all of the frog's lines and his seven wrong guesses are original.
note.rebuilt: Only the Camera Mode viewfinder is new: the remake had no client camera at the time, so the room supplies one.

rooms.title: Walk Toward the Light
rooms.offer: Pssst. You there. How are your eyes?

note.tagline: A dark room where clouds appear in coloured light.
note.about: Walk Toward the Light taught colour mixing step by step: each lesson adds a new way light can help or hinder you.
note.play: Seven lessons: timed bulbs, red walls that orbs put out, a "fall" section, and switches that mix red, yellow and blue into the colour that crosses, ending at "Astounding! You truly are a Champ!"
note.source: The five-minute limit, the solved flag at the exit door and both reward sets.
note.rebuilt: Rebuilt from the level designer's run-through, using his sign text for each lesson. Players' Snaps give the look: lamp shades throwing soft cones, bare bulbs on long wires, wooden dishes tinted by their light, red-and-pink striped poles and a plank EXIT sign.

rooms.title: We're Off to See the Lizard
quests: We're Off to See the Lizard
rooms.offer: psst, kid. hey. hey, kid. psst. hey. fuelmaking.

note.tagline: A shady deal, a fuel cell and a stranded robot.
note.about: We're Off to See the Lizard: a Shady Bureaucrat in the back alley asks you to refuel a maintenance robot stuck in a subway station.
note.play: Hear the proposition, make a Fuel Cell in a Fuelmaker, take any subway door, find the robot on the platform and refuel it.
note.source: The Bureaucrat's four lines, the three-minute alley clock, the robot's lines and the rewards.
note.rebuilt: The alley is laid out from a player's Snap of the meeting: a dark forest, a tall pale brick wall, a shaft of light, the Bureaucrat before a small grey hut and a fallen red log on the path, all from Tiny Speck's own forest pieces. The subway platform is rebuilt from two subway recordings; the remake has no subway network, so any subway door opens it.

designers.about: Level designer and scripter at Tiny Speck. Posted as LT_IndieGameDev on YouTube in 2012.

seasons.label: Zilloween
seasons.window: October 17 to November 1, and Remember 25-37 on the Dametime calendar
seasons.blurb: Jack-O-Lanterns glow on every street. Carve pumpkins with a Pick and a Knife & Board, light them with a full Firefly Jar, eat candy for a Sugar Rush, and give candy away.

facts.label: Carve
facts.text: Carve a Pumpkin with a Pick and a Knife & Board for 15 energy. Each one comes out with one of five faces, plus 5 Roasted Pepitas and a Clump of Jellisac.

facts.label: Light
facts.text: Light a carved pumpkin with a full Firefly Jar (7 fireflies), place it at home and teach it phrases to say. Carved pumpkins rot when Zilloween ends.

facts.label: Candy
facts.text: The Jack-O-Lanterns on the streets answer Trick or treat once a game day. Candy gives a Sugar Rush, 11 a game day at most (the last one brings toothache), or give it to Piggies, Chickens, Butterflies and Street Spirits.

facts.label: Grow
facts.text: Pumpkin Seeds only grow during Zilloween.

badges.name: Lanternerer
badges.desc: Lit and Displayed a Pumpkin Lantern

badges.name: Mini Tricksy-Treater
badges.desc: Gave Candy to 5 Lucky Candy-Munchers during Zilloween

badges.name: Pumpkin Carver
badges.desc: Carved the full collection of Pumpkins

badges.name: Minor Tricksy-Treater
badges.desc: Gave Candy to 37 Lucky Candy-Eaters during Zilloween

badges.name: Major Tricksy-Treater
badges.desc: Gave Candy to 103 Lucky Candy-Biters during Zilloween

badges.name: Super Tricksy-Treater
badges.desc: Gave Candy to 257 Lucky Candy-Lovers during Zilloween

badges.name: The Candyglitch
badges.desc: Gave Candy to 499 Lucky Candy-Lickers during Zilloween

seasons.label: Glitchmas
seasons.blurb: Snow over Ur and candy canes by the signposts. The Toy Vendor stocks Glitchmas Crackers and Cards, Egg Nog is back, and somebody wants you to say "yay".

facts.label: Shop
facts.text: The Toy Vendor sells Glitchmas Crackers (550 currants) and Glitchmas Cards (220 currants). Pull a cracker with a nearby critter’s help for a joke or a fun fact; sign a card and mail it.

facts.label: Quest
facts.text: A Holiday Thing: All you have to do is type "yay" into local chat and you will get a gift. The present holds a Collectors' Edition 2010 Glitchmas Yeti.

facts.label: Nog
facts.text: Nog an Egg once a game day for 11 iMG. From December 24 the Glitchmas Yeti mails you a cracker.

seasons.label: Pi Day
seasons.window: March 14, wherever it is still March 14
seasons.blurb: Anyone with a Frying Pan can cook Pi today, and a Pi in your pack can Estimate Pi for favor with Tii.

facts.label: Cook
facts.text: Cook Pi in a Frying Pan from 14 Flour, 7 Butterfly Butter, 3 Old(er) Spice and 22 Tiite. The recipe only works on Pi Day.

facts.label: Estimate
facts.text: With a Pi in your pack, Estimate Pi once a game day. Each digit you get is favor with Tii the first time each year, and mood after that.

seasons.label: Egg Hunt
seasons.blurb: Pet an Egg Plant and now and then a chocolate egg drops. Collect all five kinds and the Egg Hunter Trophy takes them in exchange.

facts.label: Pet
facts.text: Pet an Egg Plant once a game day for a 10% chance of a chocolate egg, rising to 15%, 20% and 30% with Light Green Thumb I, II and III. Without the skill only 60% of pettings take. Each of the five eggs is as likely, and they drop all year.

facts.label: Trophy
facts.text: Collect all five and the Egg Hunter Trophy takes one of each in exchange.

recent.text: Paid furniture styles sell for currants, 1,000 a credit
Furniture styles: the 113 free upgrades in Decorate, the paid ones shown locked, and Bonus Furniture Upgrade I to III
Better Learning keeps 2011's proportions: each rank takes a tenth of its 2011 time
The last four unclassified street projects are judged (G15)
Better Learning I to V return with their 2011 learn times and discounts, without the 2011 skill limit
The AFLC Frog brings express mail and the Mail Dispatcher sends parcels
Two caterpillar coats, a carnival belt and a looser glitchfashion shirt join the wardrobe
The Magic Rock stops offering Manor Mystery, a quest the original never finished
The icon test allows the Greeter Badge, left out of the catalog by decision
The top bar groups you, progress and wallet, with mood and energy stacked beside your name
Neighbours on your signpost, Note Poles, furniture for sale and restoring a friend's cultivations
A Code page that measures the three repos from git, and a CONTRIBUTING.md
Snaps between players, and the Camera takes you to them
Shared fox preserves, Fox Flurrier and trade requests in multiplayer
Speech bubbles keep off players' heads, fit their line and name only players
The live site's built pages carry the header menu's Play link
A street on the Map offers Set as Destination and Teleport Here, as the original did
A release process: live.json names what groddleafternoon.com runs, kinsta.sh deploys exactly that
tools/deploy/kinsta.sh deploys the site to groddleafternoon.com
The game connects to the realtime server the site names
Multiplayer characters from before bags get their starter bags
In multiplayer an owner on an upper house floor no longer shares the ground floor's street
The last six missing items: a Water Cooler's cup, Shim Shiri's Light Beams, the golgi apparatus, house floors and the larger Petrified Rocks
New players finish their character from the emailed link, and the bag quest says how many bags it still wants
